decision: Redesign approach + 4 human-gated decisions locked before code (per START 'propose + stop for approval'): (1) SCHEMA — additive-extend operator-triage/v0 with resolution[] + asserted_at + proven_live + provenance_source (no renames/removals; CLI + agent brief + dashboard unaffected; reversible). (2) AUDIT CADENCE — audit F001 (the contract every renderer reads) alone, then batch F002-F005 and F006-F008 (~3 paid codex calls). (3) ARCHITECTURE PLACEMENT — under Work (three clean domains; promotable later if usage shows cold visits). (4) WORKFLOW — pause for human review after F001 before building visual phases. Spec is docs/design/operator-console-redesign.md.

F001 cross-model audit (codex, the one dedicated F001 call per the locked cadence) returned needs_changes with 3 findings, all valid and fixed: (HIGH/agent-parity) the CLI/agent brief whitelisted only old fields, dropping resolution/asserted_at/proven_live/provenance_source — exactly the load-bearing redesign rule; added them to operator_brief._ITEM_FIELDS and verified the brief now carries all 4 at parity. (MEDIUM/test) a tautological resolution assertion replaced with a concrete agent_runnable->['run'] check. (LOW/spec) the spec's own JSON example used 'changes' instead of the contracted 'request_changes'. Resolved operator-style (no 2nd paid audit, per one-paid-call discipline); verified by full sweep 4060 passed + live brief-parity check. Lesson: agent parity must be VERIFIED at every renderer (brief, CLI, dashboard), not asserted — the redesign's core invariant was silently broken by a pre-existing field whitelist.

Human review blocked F001 sign-off on one render-truth defect: proven_live (= run_state in {running,conflicted}) overstated trust — a live supervisor proves the PLAN is live, not that the specific item/finding is current, so a filled freshness dot driven by it would mislabel plan-level liveness as item-level freshness. RESOLUTION: dropped the proven_live boolean entirely; replaced with typed freshness_basis ('live_supervisor_plan_match' | 'item_probe' | null). v0 emits only the plan-level basis or null; 'item_probe' (item-level proof) is RESERVED and emitted by no v0 producer. RENDER CONTRACT documented: the filled freshness dot is reserved for 'item_probe', so in v0 the dot is hollow everywhere and plan liveness can never be mislabeled. Also per review: contract note now states resolution[] enumerates resolution INTENTS, not executable commands — renderers map intents through the governed affordance/action layer (F003/F005), never inferring executable buttons from strings. Chose a single typed enum over keeping proven_live+basis: a boolean would just mirror run_state and re-tempt the overclaim. Tests: freshness_basis null/plan-match cases + an explicit guard that no v0 item ever claims item_probe. Verified operator-style (no 2nd paid audit): 43 operator suite + full sweep green; brief carries freshness_basis, not proven_live.

F002 tokens shipped as an ADDITIVE, namespaced layer (tokens.css loaded before core.css) so existing pages render pixel-identically — the redesign tokens use new/namespaced names (--bucket-*, --freshness-*, --scope-*, --run-*, --dp-*) and NEVER redefine core.css's legacy names (--surface-1, --border, --font-sans). data-theme (dark default + light) + data-density (comfort default + dense) on :root drive the whole system; lib/tokens.js is the controller. The spec's 'no raw hex in components' rule is enforced on the NEW redesign component layer (dashboard/components/, where F003+ cards/rows land) — NOT retroactively on legacy stylesheets (they share common Slate hexes like #E2E8F0/#EF4444 and are migrated onto tokens in F006). Trade-off: the existing console is NOT yet themed to light/comfort-dense — only the redesign layer is; full migration is F006. Per the locked cadence, F002 is in the F002-F005 batch audit (no codex call now); verified by 38 token assertions + 1097 full-suite green.
